moodReason: Monday's sharp rebound was driven by Nvidia's return of Jensen Huang as CEO, but Nvidia was falling again Tuesday morning and the AI-bust fears that drove last week's correction have not fully cleared.

stories.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and the stock soars 31%, lifting the major indexes
stories.what: Nvidia brought back Jensen Huang as chief executive after his earlier ouster. Its shares rose 31% on Monday, Nov 23, and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posted their best days since April 2025.
stories.why: Nvidia carries a very large weight in the major indexes and in AI-linked trades, so a leadership reversal that restores investor confidence can move the whole market.

stories.headline: Nvidia shares slide again Tuesday as uncertainty about AI stocks returns
stories.what: Nvidia traded at $156.36, down 5.26% as of 9:50 a.m. ET on Nov 24, according to Motley Fool, which attributed the drop to growing uncertainty about the future of AI stocks.
stories.why: A sharp reversal in the market's largest AI name after Monday's rally suggests the rebound may be fragile, and it could pull the Nasdaq back down at the open.

stories.headline: AI-bust fears produced the worst week for stocks since early in the pandemic for the Dow and Nasdaq
stories.what: Fortune reported that the Dow and Nasdaq had their biggest weekly declines since early COVID days and the S&P 500 had its steepest weekly drop since April 2025. Fears started after the midterm elections and were tied to the Nvidia scandal and reports that China had backdoor access to high-end US chips.
stories.why: A large drawdown raises the stakes for any further AI-related news, and the chip-access reports add a policy and national security risk to the AI trade.

stories.headline: Prediction markets lean toward a Fed rate hike rather than a cut at the Dec 9 meeting
stories.what: The Fed held rates in October, and the fed funds target range is 3.75% to 4.00%. Kalshi pricing for the Dec 9 meeting points to a hike as the more likely outcome, while a cut looks unlikely. Snapshots from different times showed different probabilities, so exact odds are not stated here.
stories.why: Expectations of higher rates tighten financial conditions and weigh on long-duration growth stocks, which is a headwind after a week of heavy losses.

watch.item: Nvidia's trading after its post-rebound slide, which will test whether Monday's rally holds
US stock markets closed for Thanksgiving
Black Friday; US stock markets close early at 1 p.m. ET
Federal Reserve meeting, with rate hike odds in focus

bottomLine: US stocks had a violent swing, with a near 5% gain in the S&P 500 on Monday after a correction, but the rebound rests heavily on Nvidia's leadership news and the stock was already falling again Tuesday. The AI-bust fears that drove the sell-off have not been resolved. Rate expectations have shifted toward a possible hike, which is a headwind for growth stocks. Investors should watch whether Nvidia can hold its gains into the short holiday week.
